blocks.text: The nervous system is the most important system for homeostasis: it regulates the other systems and also maintains homeostasis by itself. The basic elements of homeostasis work through it as follows.

items: Receptors: organs, tissues or cells such as the eyes, ears and skin that detect stimuli, changes in the external and internal environment. They act as transducers, generating nerve impulses in sensory neurons, which carry them to the central nervous system.

Central nervous system: the control centre, the brain and spinal cord, made of associative neurons (inter-neurons). They receive impulses from sensory neurons, process them and send impulses to effectors through motor neurons.
Effectors: muscles and glands that respond to impulses from the CNS, muscles by contracting and glands by secreting.

blocks.title: Receptors are transducers
blocks.text: A transducer converts one form of energy into another. Rod and cone cells in the retina, for example, convert light energy into nerve impulses (electrochemical energy).
So the path of a message in nervous coordination is: receptor, sensory neuron, CNS (inter-neurons), motor neuron, effector. Along this path the neurons are the functional units.
